elapsed.text: It was not long ago. The ground is still turned.
The grass has started to come back over it.
Long enough that you had stopped walking this way on purpose.
Long enough that you have to think about the face.
Long enough that you had stopped counting the days.

first_visit: You stand at it a while. Nobody says very much.
Someone starts a sentence about them and does not finish it.
It is a poor marker. It is the one they got.
You clear the growth off it. It will be back.
return_visit: You come back past. It is still here, which is the whole of the news.
Nothing has changed. You did not expect it to.
Somebody has left a stone on it. Not one of yours.
inheritance: They told you this once, and you had not thought about it since.
You remember them explaining it badly. It makes sense now.
It was their book. Somebody may as well carry it.
reinforced: You talk about them for a while. Everything you were carrying sits a little firmer.
lonely: There is nobody left to say anything, so you say it yourself.

burial._comment: D363 (doug-md's play-test 2 ask, D118: a companion's death shown, with a small burial). After a fight on the ground, each of the company who died for good is laid down where they fell under a cairn (`art`), with one `laid` line for them and one `said` by the lead; `after` closes it. {name} is the dead, {lead} the lead. Read by area_scene._bury. Inferred: every line, and the cairn standing in for a grave of its own (A66).
laid: They lay {name} down where they fell, and raise what stones there are over them.
There is no time for more than a shallow grave and a few stones. {name} gets both.
They close {name}'s eyes, and dig with what they have, and pile the stones high enough to be found again.
said: Rest, {name}. We'll carry the rest of it.
We'll come back this way. We'll stop.
Somebody should say something. I don't know what. You'd have known.
You'd have hated this. Too quiet, and nobody arguing.
burial.after: The grave is on the map now. Walking back to it is worth doing.
